title: Why Don't Airplane Tires Explode on Landing?
description:
In nineteen eighty-six, a Boeing seven twenty-seven took off from Mexico City. Minutes later, one of its tires exploded inside the wheel well, and the plane was lost with everyone on board. The tire was filled with ordinary air. Today, the tires on every big airliner are filled with something else. Why? And why don't airplane tires explode when they slam into the runway at more than one hundred fifty miles an hour? Today, ten landing gear secrets hidden in plain sight.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 10 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:31 1. The gas inside the tires
3:23 2. The plugs that melt
5:04 3. The straight grooves
6:27 4. The shiny piston
8:02 5. The scissors on the gear
9:39 6. The brakes that glow
11:15 7. The anti-skid
12:56 8. The puff of smoke
14:28 9. The red flags
16:03 10. The backup that uses gravity
17:36 The verdict

Sources:
- Nitrogen in tires on braked wheels above 75,000 lb, max 5% oxygen: 14 CFR 25.733(e) https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/14/25.733
- Mexicana Flight 940 (1986), air-filled tire explosion, AD 87-08-09: Wikipedia, "Mexicana de Aviación Flight 940" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexicana_de_Aviaci%C3%B3n_Flight_940
- Fusible plugs in aircraft wheels: SKYbrary, "Fusible Plug" https://skybrary.aero/articles/fusible-plug
- Boeing 737NG main tire rating (225 mph): Boeing Shop, Goodyear Flight Leader H44.5x16.5-21 https://shop.boeing.com/cpd/bdi_441k82-1=0t
- Oleo strut principle, Vickers 1915 patent: Wikipedia, "Oleo strut" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oleo_strut
- 747-8 rejected takeoff test (975,000 lb, worn brakes, 5-minute wait): AVweb, "Boeing's Takeoff Torture Test" https://www.avweb.com/news/boeings-takeoff-torture-test
- Maxaret anti-skid (Dunlop, early 1950s, ~30% shorter stops, Jensen FF): Wikipedia, "Maxaret" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxaret
- Tire nitrogen and inflation guidance: FAA AC 20-97B https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC20-97B.pdf
